verdict.rationale: The evidence pack draws repeatedly from a first-party GitHub repository (github.com/gnachman/iTerm2), and community reports describe public upstream commits that an outsider read and fed to an LLM. That indicates the source is publicly readable. However, no evidence names the license or confirms it is an open-source license. Missing for 10: explicit statement of an open license (e.g., GPL), first-party docs pointing to the source repo, and confirmation the full app source is in that repo.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: built an exploit just by prompting an LLM with the upstream iTerm2 commit
fix was committed upstream but hadn't yet reached stable releases
